You said: spam-techniciansspam-technicians
Tech support scams involve fraudsters pretending to be technicians from well-known companies like Microsoft, Apple, or antivirus providers to steal your money or personal data. [1, 2]
How the Scam Works

* Fake Pop-Ups: Intrusive browser warnings flash on your screen claiming your device is infected and urging you to call a toll-free number immediately.
* Cold Calls: Scammers call or text out of the blue, claiming they detected a virus or a security breach on your network.
* Remote Access Request: They trick you into installing remote-desktop software so they can "fix" the fake problem, giving them free rein over your files and bank accounts. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

How to Protect Yourself

* Never Call the Number: Real security alerts from Windows or macOS will never display a phone number for you to call.
* Do Not Grant Access: Never allow remote access to your computer or phone to anyone who contacted you unsolicited.
* Force Quit and Restart: If a freezing pop-up appears in your browser, close the browser window or restart your computer entirely. [1, 2, 3]

What to Do If You Were Targeted

* Report It: File a report with the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
* Secure Accounts: Change your passwords immediately if you gave a scammer any login credentials.
* Contact Your Bank: Call your financial institution right away if you shared financial details or authorized a transfer. [1, 2]

If you want, tell me:

* How did they contact you (pop-up, phone call, or email)?
* Did you give them remote access or send any money/gift cards?

I can give you exact steps to secure your device right now.
